shots.text: (recap — Part 1 clips)
Now it's back.
The shadow rises... pale green.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: A wide, flat head. A mouth...
shots.subject: other

shots.text: ...a back covered in white spots
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo grabs the knife. Mara puts her hand on his arm.
No rows of teeth. Just a wide open filter.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: It's a whale shark...
shots.subject: other

shots.text: ...feeds on plankton and tiny fish
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Divers say whale sharks are often curious.
A slow circle around the raft...
shots.subject: other

shots.text: ...and sinks back into the blue.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo lets out a breath.
I think it was just saying hello.
The storm taught them two things.
Mara ties them in triangles.
Every piece connected to two others.
Side-on to the waves...
And that's how rafts flip. / A simple tool for exactly this.
A sea anchor.
...far less likely to capsize.
They don't have one. So they build one.
They throw it overboard.
...steady as a weather vane.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo stares. That's it?
That's all it takes, Mara says.
'I told you so' / Teo lets her have it.
They've survived the storm. Food under the raft.
Rain is unpredictable.
Mara remembers a science class.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Trap the vapor under a clear surface.
It's called a solar still.
Bottle, plastic, a dark container.
Then they wait. An hour later...
A single drop.
Steven Callahan, 1982.
Hard to get working. A small amount.
A clock that's ticking... or stopped.
They're making their own water.
Days turn into weeks. The raft becomes something else.
Teo builds a roof from the tarp.
Mara strings a line, fish to dry.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo plants a coconut.
He waters it anyway. 'Morale.'
Below the raft, something is happening too.
Small fish... and bigger fish.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Callahan's raft turned into a tiny reef.
Living on top of an ecosystem.
The horizon.
Every morning, the same flat line.
Day 26. Teo wants a sail, steer west.
Mara: too risky.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: 'So we just sit here? Forever?'
Mara turns away.
For the rest of the day... not a single word.
That night, Teo can't sleep.
She points to a single star.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: 'Polaris. The North Star.'
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Star height = your latitude.
Mara stacks her fist up to the star.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: For the first time in 26 days...
'I'm sorry.' 'Me too.'
Five days later, Teo sees it first.
A dot. A shape. A ship.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: A huge cargo ship, 2–3 miles away.
They scream. They wave.
Mara flashes sunlight off plastic.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The ship keeps moving.
A shape again. A dot. Nothing.
One of the cruelest things...
A speck among waves and glare.
Callahan: ships passed. Not one stopped.
Teo sits on the edge. Stares.
Mara sits down beside him.
'Turn around.'
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo turns. He really looks at it.
A roof. A water still. Drying fish.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: A sea anchor. A sail. A coconut.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: 18 pieces of wood, tied in triangles.
A month ago, one plank. Now, a home.
Teo is quiet for a long time.
He measures a new plank. 'What are you doing?'
'If the world won't find us... we'll build one.'
What would you build first?

lines: THE LARGEST FISH IN THE OCEAN
most accounts say nine — none stopped

That's it? That's all it took?
If you have it before the storm.
So we just sit here? Forever?
If the world won't find us...
